16861fc22e4a9476: NOVEMBER 27 — When Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this morning, he did so for the swearing-in of the state executive council (exco). Not to witness the swearing-in of a new Menteri Besar. He remains as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan. That means he has the confidence of the majority of the members of the State Legislative Assembly (SLA) as required by Article 38(2)(a) of the State Constitution 1959. The majority must include the 10 former exco members whose appointments were revoked by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir effective September 20. In other words, Ismail has shown he still commands majority support among assemblymen which allows him to submit a list of exco members for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration. Six assemblymen were sworn in as new exco members before Tuanku Muhriz this morning. They were sworn in on advice of Ismail as the Menteri Besar in accordance with Article 38(2)(b) of the State Constitution. Be that as it may, Ismail’s command of majority support remains to be tested in the SLA when it sits to pass the state budget. But let this be said: Enough is enough! The state’s constitutional crisis has dragged on for nearly four months. That’s long enough. Do not drag it any further.

bdd7906f9f2f28b2: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded newly appointed members of the state executive council (Exco) to remain within the scope of their respective portfolios and not overstep their authority and responsibilities.
His Royal Highness said recent events and issues should serve as lessons and guidance for all parties, particularly Exco members entrusted with the responsibility of administering the state.
“Focus your full attention on the portfolios entrusted to you and discharge your responsibilities with commitment and wisdom.

“I do not wish to see a recurrence of past events that could undermine the harmony, stability, and smooth administration of the state government,” Tuanku Muhriz said at the appointment and swearing-in ceremony for the Negeri Sembilan Exco members at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.

Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.

The ceremony was also attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid; Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.

Tuanku Muhriz further reminded the Exco members to put the people’s interests first, uphold the highest standards of integrity and professionalism, and ensure that every decision made serves the best interests of the state and the well-being of its people.

His Royal Highness also congratulated the elected representatives appointed to the state executive council, describing their appointments as an honour that carries significant responsibilities and a great trust towards the state and its people.

He also prayed that the Menteri Besar and all Exco members would be granted the guidance, strength, and wisdom needed to discharge their responsibilities and ensure that Negeri Sembilan remains peaceful, prosperous, and progressive.
Earlier, six state assemblymen took their oaths of office as new members of the Negeri Sembilan Exco before Tuanku Muhriz.
The appointments mark a change in the composition of the state administration following recent political developments in Negeri Sembilan.
In the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 18 of the 36 state seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven seats. — Bernama

63fd899b752a022e: WELLINGTON: Fifteen months after spotting a job ad seeking a new leader for a political party, Qiulae Wong will help decide New Zealand's next government after Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition lost its majority.
The 38-year-old former KPMG consultant took over a party polling at about 1%in August last year.

Since then, the Opportunity Party has secured seven seats and 6.1% of the vote in this month's election, placing it in prime position to play kingmaker as Luxon rushes to piece together a workable coalition.
Wong preaches "pragmatic politics" as a counter to growing polarisation, saying she wants to "bring the heat down a little bit and actually just focus on moving the country forward".
Establishment parties worldwide have been losing support in recent elections, replaced by a surge in populist movements touting more radical policies on the left or right.
But Wong, who is of Chinese and European descent and was born in Fiji, said following the election she believed the result showed voters were tiring of that kind of politics.
"I think we are seeing a push globally for more pragmatic politics," she told journalists.
"We've seen that populism doesn't deliver results," she said.
"It is paper thin; it doesn't have substance around taking countries forward.
"So it's really encouraging to have had that support."
Ardern 2.0?
Wong worked in sustainable fashion before entering politics.
A mother of two, her social media emphasises her ordinariness -- moving effortlessly from pints in the sun and ice creams with the kids to political rallies and media events.
All that has prompted comparisons to former prime minister Jacinda Ardern, whose star power made her a global progressive icon.

"I think the way in which both of those two relatively young women are attempting a different style of politics is something that marks Wong apart," Massey University politics professor Richard Shaw told AFP.
He said Opportunity's rise had been "remarkable", given its differences to other New Zealand political parties and due to the relative inexperience of Wong.

"At a time when the politics of this country are becoming more fraught and more feral and more shouty, and there is horrendous online trolling of women in public life, you've got this woman who's coming in saying 'I'm leading a party and we're going to do it this way'.
"I think that appeals to people."
Tricky negotiations
Luxon had previously ruled out working with Opportunity.
He now faces an embarrassing volte-face, admitting Friday he will need the centrist outsiders' support if he wants to stay in office.
All eyes are now on Wong as the country faces weeks of political wrangling.
She has said she will work with Luxon -- but insisted that her party's "bottom lines" are non-negotiable.

Those lines -- on climate change action, regulations on political lobbying, healthcare reform, phasing out bottom trawling, and cost of living -- could be a hard sell in talks with Luxon's right-wing partners, the populist NZ First and libertarian ACT.

On the campaign trail, she also ruled out working with a government in which NZ First leader Winston Peters was foreign minister, after he told a Chinese-born lawmaker to "go back to your own country".
And on Friday she refused to rule out taking the country back for a second election if talks don't work out.
"All we can do is be as constructive and proactive as possible to make this happen. But it's not just us around the table," she said.

47c14df4bba2f9a1: KULAI: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission's lawsuit against Google over its alleged failure to tackle harmful content on YouTube has been served on the company's lawyers in Malaysia, deputy communications minister Teo Nie Ching said.
Teo said this was MCMC's first lawsuit against Google, although it had previously taken legal action against Telegram.
"To my knowledge, the suit has been served on Google through its lawyers in Malaysia," she told reporters after attending a programme at SK Murni Jaya here today.
She said YouTube's weak content screening system had forced MCMC to deploy its own staff to monitor and report online gambling content, when Google should have its own team to handle the task.
MCMC said 74,703 reports had been submitted to YouTube between Jan 1 and Oct 28, of which 74,569, or 99.8%, concerned online gambling.
On Nov 25, MCMC announced that it had filed two lawsuits against Google, seeking a total of RM600 million in damages.
The first suit alleges that Google failed to take reasonable steps to address harmful content, including online gambling and scams.
The second concerns the republication of content by blogger Papagomo, which allegedly breached the law.
MCMC is seeking RM300 million in each suit, comprising RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages.
cf1949faf59ead69: SEOUL, Nov 27 — South Korea repatriated six North Koreans today after they were found drifting in international waters on a fishing boat earlier this month, Seoul’s unification ministry said.
The announcement came following heightened tensions along the heavily fortified border, after a recent mine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ).
The boat, initially carrying seven North Koreans, was found drifting in international waters off South Korea’s Ulleungdo island on November 3 and towed by the military and coast guard.

Authorities decided to repatriate six on humanitarian grounds after confirming their wishes through a series of inquiries involving government agencies and the United Nations Command, according to authorities.
One of the North Koreans expressed a wish to stay and will remain in the South, according to the ministry.

The fishing boat carrying the six North Koreans on Friday crossed the Northern Limit Line (NLL), the de facto maritime border, in the East Sea—also known as the Sea of Japan—under its own power at 8:33 KST (2333 GMT), the ministry said.
It then joined a North Korean vessel waiting north of the boundary and continued northwards, according to Seoul’s Yonhap news agency.
The UNC is believed to have notified Pyongyang of the repatriation plan in advance, as it did last year, according to Yonhap.
The presence of a North Korean vessel suggests Pyongyang received the notification, although no response from the North has been reported, Yonhap added.

Under Seoul’s constitution, all North Koreans are considered citizens of the Republic of Korea, as the South is officially known, and those who reach its territory and seek to defect are generally allowed to stay.
North Korea is known to brutally retaliate against defectors and their families.

Seoul carried out a similar repatriation last year, returning two North Korean vessels and all their occupants in accordance with their wishes after they were rescued in separate incidents in March and May. — AFP
adcd8516c1199487: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Media Prima Audio Nazri Noran bertanggungjawab atas video kontroversi dua DJ FlyFM, Ean Nasrun dan Adam Raqeem, yang dilihat ‘bersolat’ untuk Manchester United yang sedang dilanda krisis.
Nazri berkata beliau turut menegur kedua-dua penyampai radio itu dan mengingatkan mereka supaya tidak menggunakan unsur agama dalam kandungan mereka.
Dalam kenyataan, Nazri berkata orang ramai berhak mengkritik kedua-dua DJ terbabit berhubung video dengan kapsyen ‘Praying for Man United’ itu.
“Solat adalah ibadah. Jangan jadikannya bahan kandungan. Kita sepatutnya lebih tahu,” katanya dalam video permohonan maaf bersama Ean dan Adam berhubung kontroversi itu.
Beliau mengingatkan Ean dan Adam bahawa tugas mereka adalah untuk menghiburkan pendengar, selain menggesa mereka memberi tumpuan kepada pekerjaan tanpa menyentuh sensitiviti agama.
“Fokus sahaja untuk menghiburkan. Itu tugas kamu. Perkara lain tidak perlu dibawa masuk. Jangan libatkan agama.”
Nazri memuji kesediaan Ean dan Adam mengakui kesilapan mereka, namun mengingatkan kejadian itu tidak boleh berulang.
“Kita tidak sepatutnya perlu membincangkan perkara ini lagi,” katanya.
Ean mengakui penghasilan video itu satu kesilapan dan memohon maaf, sambil berkata mereka tidak sepatutnya menggunakan agama sebagai bahan kandungan.
Beliau turut berterima kasih kepada orang ramai yang mengkritik mereka, sambil mengakui mereka mempunyai sebab untuk berasa tersinggung.
Ean berkata tiada alasan bagi mempertahankan perbuatan itu dan beliau bersedia menerima sebarang tindakan terhadap mereka.
“Apa pun tindakan yang diputuskan terhadap kami, itu wajar,” katanya.
Sementara itu, Adam mengakui mereka tidak menggunakan sewajarnya platform yang diberikan untuk menghiburkan orang ramai.
Beliau berkata tidak tahu apa lagi yang hendak dikatakan berhubung kontroversi itu, malah turut ditegur ibunya sendiri kerana video berkenaan.
“Ini kali pertama dan terakhir,” katanya sambil berjanji tidak akan mengulangi kesilapan itu.
Ean turut memohon maaf bagi pihak kedua-dua DJ terbabit dan FlyFM, sambil mengakui insiden itu memberi kesan kepada stesen radio berkenaan, pihak pengurusan serta keluarga mereka.
Respons menteri hal ehwal agama
Dalam kenyataan, Menteri Hal Ehwal Agama Zulkifli Hasan berkata solat adalah antara rukun Islam dan merupakan ibadah suci.
Katanya, solat tidak seharusnya dipandang remeh atau dijadikan bahan jenaka, hiburan murahan mahupun parodi.

Zulkifli turut mengingatkan pengamal media dan pencipta kandungan supaya menjaga sensitiviti agama serta mematuhi garis panduan penyiaran demi memelihara keharmonian masyarakat berbilang kaum dan agama di negara ini.
Katanya, kebebasan bersuara dan berkarya bukan alasan untuk mempersendakan ibadah atau menyentuh perkara asas akidah sehingga boleh mencetuskan kemarahan orang ramai dan menggugat ketenteraman awam.

Zulkifli turut menggesa pengurusan stesen radio itu memastikan pihak terbabit segera memadam kandungan berkenaan, memohon maaf secara terbuka kepada umat Islam serta memastikan kejadian sama tidak berulang.
e6780a21087af4a4: HANOI: Vietnam said on Thursday it was working with the US to complete a trade deal as soon as possible hours after the Trump administration threatened new tariffs that could hurt key export industries, from clothing and footwear and electronics.

The manufacturing hub, which runs the largest trade surplus of any US partner, faces potential rates of 35% on grounds of excessive industrial capacity, exceeding those of Southeast Asian peers and second only to China's among the 14 targeted.

Shortly after the tariffs were unveiled, Vietnam's trade ministry said the two countries were working to seal a trade deal "as soon as possible", adding that it would cooperate with the US investigation on excessive capacity.
Vietnam, home to major export operations of multinationals including Samsung Electronics and Apple, has spent more than a year hammering out a trade deal with Washington.
Industry officials, who expected an agreement in December, when Vietnam leader To Lam is set to attend a G20 summit in Florida, see the new tariff threat as an inducement to reach a deal.

"I would not rule out a deal over the coming months," said Bruno Jaspaert, the head of DEEP C Industrial Zones, a network of industrial parks in northern Vietnam hosting export-oriented factories run by multinational companies.

Such a trade deal could leave Vietnam with tariffs of 20%, above an existing general duty of 12.5% and slightly higher than regional competitors but well below the threatened 35%, US officials have said.
That would keep Vietnamese tariffs significantly below those on China, preserving its appeal to foreign investors as an alternative manufacturing base nearby.
Footwear, clothing hit
Months of tariff uncertainty may have already hurt some sectors since production shifted elsewhere as orders dropped, Jaspaert added.
"Most of the industries facing the highest threats may have already made plans and carried out contingency measures," he said.

The planned new US tariff "adds uncertainty for manufacturers serving the American market and could delay sourcing and expansion decisions," said John Campbell, head of industrial services in Vietnam at real estate firm Savills.
"Garments, textiles and footwear producers with significant US exposure would be particularly sensitive to higher costs and pressure on margins," he said.

Officials of the footwear industry have said Indonesia has attracted new investment, while expansion has stalled in Vietnam, home to large operations for Nike NKE.N, Adidas ADSGn.DE and other leading shoemakers.
Competitors in apparel and footwear such as Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia, have struck deals with Washington for tariffs of 18%.
Electronic woes

Vietnam also faces a US investigation into accusations of intellectual property violations, with a Feb 28 deadline. Washington has also accused it of functioning as a transit point for Chinese goods headed to the US.
The accusation is particularly ominous for Vietnam's electronics industry, which uses large volumes of Chinese-made components to assemble devices such as computers, tablets and video game consoles.
Samsung and Tesla were among companies that urged the US government not to increase tariffs on Vietnam over intellectual property, arguing that would hurt supply chains.
Vietnam pledged to tackle issues raised in US trade investigations in a resolution published just hours before the US unveiled the new tariffs.

It said it would review reliance on imported inputs, develop domestic supply sources and build a database to monitor manufacturers' supply chains. The government also pledged to establish an early-warning mechanism to manage trade surpluses.

b24d86a045538de6: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The launch of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) master plan has been postponed for a second time, with a new date yet to be set.
Johor menteri besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the plan was meant to be launched at a meeting in December between the leaders of Malaysia and Singapore, following the initial postponement in March.
He said the master plan document had been ready since March, and the state government had called for its launch to be expedited.

"In an increasingly competitive global economic landscape, we do not want this delay to cause Johor to lose momentum and investment opportunities," he said in his winding-up speech on Johor's 2027 budget at the state legislative assembly sitting here today.
The master plan, prepared by the Iskandar Regional Development Authority in partnership with the economy ministry, outlines the investment direction of the JS-SEZ.
It details priority sectors, infrastructure requiring improvement and the development of a skilled workforce to support cross-border economic activities.

Malaysia and Singapore signed an agreement to establish the JS-SEZ on Jan 7, 2025. The zone encompasses nine key areas in Johor and focuses on 11 sectors, including manufacturing, logistics, the digital economy and energy.

Addressing issues raised by the assemblymen for Gambir, Bentayan and Tenang, Onn Hafiz said state development efforts also extend to areas outside the JS-SEZ, ensuring that economic opportunities can be enjoyed by all Johoreans.
To achieve this goal, the state government must strengthen economic hubs, enhance connectivity between regions and reduce barriers to economic activity, he said.
10c885b2f650ff49: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Four Barisan Nasional (BN) assemblymen and one each from Wawasan and PAS were sworn in as Negeri Sembilan executive councillors today, more than two months after the previous 10 councillors lost their posts.

Berita Harian reported that the swearing-in ceremony took place at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah, where Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim announced the six appointments approved by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Umno’s three representatives are Kota assemblyman Suhaimi Aini, Senaling assemblyman Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil and Jeram Padang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir.
Repah assemblyman Koh Kim Swee of MCA takes the fourth BN seat on the council, alongside Gemas assemblyman Ridzuan Ahmad of Wawasan and Bagan Pinang assemblyman Abdul Fatah Zakaria of PAS.
The Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, also attended the ceremony.
In September, the previous councillors backed a proclamation naming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as ruler in place of Tuanku Muhriz.
Tuanku Muhriz revoked all 10 appointments on September 20, with the palace saying the councillors had breached their oaths of office.

Yesterday, after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party would leave it to the palace to announce the outcome of their discussions on the menteri besar’s position and the exco appointments.
99c17ec87fa62890: SINGAPORE, Nov 27 — Singapore has not started negotiations on an Agreement of Reciprocal Tariff (ART) with the United States (US), but remains open to talks aimed at securing a lower tariff rate, said Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.
Gan, who is also the Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Trade) said Singapore and the US had been engaging regularly over the last couple of years amid an ongoing investigation by Washington.

“With the Section 301 (of the Trade Act of 1974) investigation in process, we have also had multiple engagements and these engagements allow us to explain our positions, share our views, and put across our arguments.
“But we have not started negotiating on a trade deal,” he said at a press conference yesterday evening.

The United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday released a report on its findings and proposed actions against 14 economies, including Singapore and Malaysia, under Section 301 related to structural excess capacity and production in specific manufacturing sectors.

Commenting on the proposed tariff rates of up to 20 per cent, Gan expressed shock at the decision, saying that the US is an important trading partner of the republic, with which it shares long standing bilateral relations.

He noted that the new proposed tariffs will raise the effective tariff rate on Singapore goods from 7.8 per cent to 10.3 per cent, potentially affecting about S$9.4 billion (S$1=RM3.19) worth of Singapore exports to the US.

“We have been working together for many years, and we have a free trade agreement (FTA) with the US, so I think the tariff is a surprise to us and it is not something that we expect from a major trading partner.

“We will continue to strengthen our bilateral relationship and look forward to finding a way to resolve the differences in our tariffs and our trade relationship, and to seek a better tariff for our exporters,” he added.

On the negotiations process, Gan said Singapore has always been very principled in its engagement with trading partners by putting its interest at the centre of discussions, whether with the US or any other partner.
He stressed that the republic will continue to adopt that approach in its discussion with the US.

“We also have to bear in mind that whatever agreement we achieve with the US, there will be a give-and-take, there will be compromises, and there will be trade-offs that we will need to accept,” he said. — Bernama

9cddd48edb1446c9: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has urged the management of a private radio station to immediately remove a viral video linking Islamic prayer (solat) to English Premier League football matches and issue a public apology to the Muslim community.
In a statement posted on Facebook today, Zulkifli also called on the radio station to issue a public apology to the Muslim community and ensure that a similar incident does not recur.

He stressed that solat is a fundamental pillar of Islam and a sacred obligation for Muslims, adding that its sanctity must be respected and should never be trivialised through jokes, cheap entertainment or parody in any form of broadcasting.

“To preserve harmony in the country’s multiracial and multi-religious society, all media practitioners and content creators are reminded to remain sensitive to religious concerns and comply with established broadcasting guidelines.

“Freedom of expression and creativity do not, under any circumstances, justify mocking religious rituals or treating fundamental aspects of faith in a manner that could provoke anger and threaten public order,” he said.
Zulkifli also urged all parties to uphold proper conduct, respect the sanctity of all religions and use media platforms as tools to educate the public and promote unity.
Recently, an 11-second video titled “Praying for Man United”, uploaded by a radio station, went viral on social media.

The clip featured two men in a radio studio performing movements resembling ruku’ (bowing) and sujud (prostration), alongside the display of the football match score between Sporting CP and Manchester United.

1f03866cbbdfbba3: PETALING JAYA: Enam Adun Negeri Sembilan mengangkat sumpah sebagai exco di depan Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir di Istana Besar Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah.
Daripada jumlah itu, empat ialah Adun Barisan Nasional (BN), manakala dua lagi daripada Perikatan Nasional (PN), menurut The Star.
Adun BN terdiri daripada Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang), Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling) dan Suhaimi Aini (Kota) daripada Umno serta Koh Kim Swee daripada MCA (Repah).
Dua wakil rakyat PN ialah Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas) daripada Wawasan dan Fatah Zakaria (Bagan Pinang) daripada PAS.
Negeri Sembilan tidak mempunyai exco sejak 20 Sept lalu apabila semua 10 exco dilucutkan jawatan kerana didakwa melanggar sumpah jawatan dengan menyokong deklarasi memohon penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz.
Mereka terdiri daripada lapan Adun BN dan dua wakil rakyat PN.

Mereka ialah Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Razi Ali (Sungai Lui), Asna Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) dan Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh) daripada Umno.
Tiga lagi ialah Adun MCA Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), Fairuz Isa (Serting) daripada PAS dan Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat) daripada Wawasan.

Sepuluh Adun itu kemudiannya membawa kes mereka ke mahkamah bagi mencabar keputusan pemecatan mereka. Tetapi, mereka akhirnya menarik balik saman itu susulan dakwaan peletakan jawatan Ismail Lasim sebagai menteri besar.
Walaupun Mahkamah Tinggi Seremban menegaskan peletakan jawatan Ismail belum disahkan, 10 bekas exco itu tetap meneruskan penarikan balik saman berkenaan.
Tuanku Muhriz melucutkan pelantikan mereka susulan pendirian mereka mendakwa penyingkiran baginda April lalu adalah sah dan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar merupakan pemerintah baharu negeri itu.
Pihak istana melihat tindakan mereka bercanggah sumpah taat setia kepada pemerintah dan institusi diraja.
ee55804bdfc7d02a: PETALING JAYA: Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir mengingatkan barisan exco negeri yang baharu dilantik supaya tidak melampaui bidang kuasa masing-masing, susulan kemelut yang melanda negeri itu.
Baginda bertitah segala peristiwa dan isu yang tercetus baru-baru ini harus dijadikan pengajaran dan pedoman oleh semua pihak, khususnya anggota Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri.
“Kamu hendaklah sentiasa memahami batas tugas dan bidang kuasa masing-masing serta tidak bertindak melampaui kuasa dan tanggungjawab yang telah ditetapkan.
“Tumpukan sepenuh perhatian kepada portfolio yang diamanahkan dan laksanakan tanggungjawab tersebut dengan penuh komitmen dan kebijaksanaan.

“Beta tidak mahu perkara yang sama berulang sehingga boleh menjejaskan keharmonian, kestabilan dan kelancaran pentadbiran kerajaan negeri,” titah baginda pada istiadat pelantikan dan angkat sumpah exco di Istana Besar Seri Menanti hari ini.
Tuanku Muhriz turut mengingatkan barisan exco bahawa pelantikan mereka bukan sahaja satu penghormatan, malah membawa tanggungjawab dan amanah besar kepada negeri serta rakyat.

Baginda mahu mereka mengutamakan kepentingan rakyat, melaksanakan tanggungjawab dengan penuh integriti dan profesionalisme serta memastikan setiap keputusan berlandaskan kepentingan negeri dan kesejahteraan rakyat.

Istiadat hari ini menyusul selepas Negeri Sembilan lebih dua bulan tanpa barisan exco susulan keputusan Tuanku Muhriz membatalkan pelantikan kesemua 10 anggotanya pada 20 Sept lalu kerana melanggar ikrar taat setia kepada baginda.
Ia selepas barisan exco terbabit mengeluarkan kenyataan mengesahkan dakwaan penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar, yang kemudian disokong Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim.
Bagaimanapun, Jabatan Peguam Negara menegaskan pengumuman itu tidak mempunyai kesan undang-undang kerana menteri besar dan exco tidak mempunyai kuasa menyingkirkan Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Ismail pada 14 Nov mengesahkan menarik balik surat kepada Penyimpan Mohor Besar Raja-Raja berhubung penyingkiran Tuanku Muhriz, manakala empat hari kemudian, 10 bekas exco terbabit menarik balik saman mencabar pembatalan pelantikan mereka.
Pada 20 Nov, pihak istana memaklumkan Ismail perlu membuktikan masih mendapat sokongan majoriti Adun serta mengemukakan senarai exco untuk pertimbangan Tuanku Muhriz.

afb62b1528d01cd4: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 27 — Penang housing and environment executive councillor Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu has directed all district officers to activate their disaster management committees as forecasts warn of thunderstorms in most areas of the state tomorrow afternoon.
Sundarajoo said the Penang State Disaster Management Committee issued the directive to ensure districts could monitor flood risks and coordinate quickly with the agencies involved.

“All district officers, who chair their respective District Disaster Management Committees, have been directed to activate their committees so that preparedness measures, monitoring and inter-agency coordination can be carried out promptly and effectively,” he said in a statement today.
He said the State Disaster Management Secretariat will step up monitoring, especially at flood hotspots and other locations identified as being at risk of flooding.
“Inspections of assets and operational equipment have also been stepped up to ensure that they are in good working order and ready for deployment in the event of an emergency,” he said.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast for November 26 to 28, thunderstorms are expected in most areas of Penang in the afternoons.
Rain and thunderstorms may also occur in some areas at night.
On November 28, rain and thunderstorms are expected in some areas in the morning, with thunderstorms forecast to affect most areas in the afternoon.
Rain and thunderstorms may continue into the night.
“I wish to stress that public safety and well-being remain a priority for the state government,” Sundarajoo said.
He urged residents in low-lying areas, near rivers, along the coast and in areas frequently affected by flooding to remain vigilant and prepare in advance.
“This includes keeping important documents, medication and essential supplies ready,” he said.

He advised the public to obtain information and follow the latest weather developments and water levels through official channels, namely MetMalaysia’s myCuaca app and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage’s Public InfoBanjir portal.
He also advised the public to temporarily suspend all recreational and leisure activities involving bodies of water, including activities at rivers, beaches and water recreation areas.
He called on the public to cooperate fully with the security, rescue and disaster management agencies in any possible disaster.
2cdfc0258b211f37: PETALING JAYA: Media Prima Audio CEO Nazri Noran has taken responsibility for a controversial video by FlyFM DJs Ean Nasrun and Adam Raqeem in which they are seen "praying" for crisis-hit Manchester United.
Nazri also said he had reprimanded the DJs, telling them to keep religion out of their content.
In a statement, Nazri said people had every right to criticise the DJs for the video, captioned "Praying for Man United".
"Solat is an act of worship. Don’t use this as part of content. We should know better," he said in a video in which he, Ean and Adam apologised for the controversy.
He reminded Ean and Adam that their role was to entertain audiences and urged them to focus on their work without touching on religious sensitivities.
"Just stick to entertaining. That’s it. That’s all you do. Everything else, leave it out of context. Leave religion out of it."
Nazri praised Ean and Adam for owning up to their gaffe, but warned that it should never happen again.
"And we shouldn’t have this conversation again," he added.
Ean admitted that the video was a mistake and apologised, saying they should never have used religion as part of their content.
He also thanked members of the public who criticised them, saying they were right to be offended.
Ean said there were no excuses for what happened and that he was prepared to accept any action taken against them.
"Whatever you decide to do with us, fair," he said.
Adam, meanwhile, acknowledged that the incident was not an appropriate use of the platform they had been given to entertain the public.
He said he was lost for words over the controversy and that even his mother had reprimanded him for the video.
"First and last time," he said, vowing not to repeat the mistake.
Ean also apologised on behalf of the DJs and FlyFM, acknowledging that the incident had affected the station, its management and their families.
Religious affairs minister’s response
In a statement, religious affairs minister Zulkifli Hasan said ritual prayers were among the pillars of Islam and a sacred act.
He said prayers should never be trivialised or used for humour, cheap entertainment or parody.

Zulkifli also reminded media practitioners and content creators to be mindful of religious sensitivities and comply with broadcasting guidelines to preserve harmony in the country’s multiracial and multi-religious society.
He said freedom of expression and creativity did not justify mocking religious rituals or touching on fundamental matters of faith that could provoke public anger and threaten public order.
Zulkifli also urged the radio station’s management to ensure that those involved remove the content immediately, issue a public apology to Muslims and ensure that similar incidents do not recur.

2f1731be44c737e9: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan Johor mahu sekurang-kurangnya 25% hasil cukai disumbang kepada Putrajaya dikembalikan untuk menguruskan sendiri lebih banyak keperluan pembangunan negeri.
Menteri Besar, Onn Hafiz Ghazi, berkata kerajaan negeri turut membantu menyedia dan menaik taraf pelbagai kemudahan agensi persekutuan yang bukan tanggungjawab hakiki negeri.
Beliau memberi contoh bantuan untuk kerja membaik pulih kuarters polis di Muar, menaik taraf sekolah dan menyokong keperluan wad kecemasan serta klinik kesihatan.
Menurutnya, kerajaan negeri turut membantu pembayaran doktor locum, menaik taraf Sekolah Rintis Bangsa Johor, membaik pulih IPK, IPD, kem tentera serta Kompleks Kastam, Imigresen dan Kuarantin (CIQ).

"Kalau kita mampu, lebih banyak lagi yang mahu kerajaan negeri salurkan untuk membantu mereka yang berjuang di Johor,” katanya menurut Sinar Harian dalam ucapan penggulungan pada sidang Dewan Undangan Negeri.

Jelasnya, pendirian kerajaan negeri berhubung pemulangan hasil cukai itu seiring titah Pemangku Sultan Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail supaya sekurang-kurangnya 25% hasil cukai disumbang, dikembalikan dan diuruskan kerajaan negeri.

Jun lalu, Tunku Mahkota Ismail bertitah Johor menyumbang lebih RM40 bilion setahun kepada kerajaan persekutuan, tetapi hanya menerima sekitar RM2 bilion hingga RM3 bilion untuk memenuhi keperluan hampir lima juta penduduknya.
Baginda bertitah, sekurang-kurangnya 25% hingga 30% hasil dikutip dari Johor wajar dikembalikan kepada negeri itu bagi membolehkan lebih banyak projek pembangunan dan kebajikan rakyat dilaksanakan.
Pada Disember 2024, kerajaan negeri meminta 20% hasil cukai disalurkan semula untuk Johor mempunyai ruang kewangan lebih besar melaksanakan pembangunan.
18c33175ab1231b0: PETALING JAYA: Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR) sedang mendapatkan pengesahan daripada Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) berhubung implikasi perundangan jika Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) mendapat majoriti mudah bagi membentuk kerajaan negeri selepas selesai proses penamaan calon PRN Sarawak esok.
Pengerusi SPR, Ramlan Harun, berkata ia masih dalam penelitian AGC bagi memastikan sebarang tindakan atau keputusan mematuhi peraturan pilihan raya sedia ada.

Beliau berkata, semua proses pilihan raya yang ditetapkan perlu diteruskan berdasarkan peraturan semasa manakala sebarang pengumuman berhubung dengan isu itu hanya akan dibuat selepas SPR memperoleh pengesahan pihak berkaitan.
"Saya sudah minta perkara ini disemak dengan pihak AGC dan perkara ini masih lagi dalam semakan. Ada peraturan-peraturan berkaitan yang perlu kita patuhi.

"Kalau berdasarkan peraturan sedia ada, kita kena lihat semua proses pilihan raya ini terpaksa juga dijalankan, mesti dijalankan dan sebarang pengumuman akan dibuat selepas itu," katanya, menurut Harian Metro.
Beliau berkata demikian pada sidang media selepas meninjau persiapan hari penamaan calon PRN Sarawak di Pusat Penamaan Calon Samariang di Kuching.
Ramlan berkata kesemua 82 pusat penamaan calon di seluruh negeri bersedia menerima calon dari 9 pagi hingga 10 pagi esok.

GPS menamakan calon bagi kesemua 82 kerusi, diikuti Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak dengan 26 calon, Parti Bumi Kenyalang dan DAP masing-masing 12 calon, Parti Bangsa Malaysia dengan seorang calon serta seorang calon bebas.
Daripada 82 kerusi itu, sebanyak 44 kerusi kini hanya mempunyai seorang calon, manakala 36 kerusi mempunyai dua calon dan dua lagi mempunyai tiga calon.

Semalam, kumpulan masyarakat sivil Sarawak, Persatuan Pemangkin Daya Masyarakat atau ROSE, membangkitkan kebimbangan bahawa hampir separuh daripada 82 kawasan pilihan raya negeri itu mungkin tidak ditandingi susulan keputusan beberapa parti politik nasional untuk tidak menyertai pilihan raya berkenaan.
ROSE berkata anggaran awal menunjukkan hanya kira-kira 38 kerusi akan ditandingi, sekali gus berpotensi membolehkan GPS memenangi sehingga 44 kerusi tanpa bertanding.

Barisan Nasional (BN), PAS dan Bersatu memutuskan untuk tidak bertanding dalam pilihan raya itu. Dengan PKR dan Amanah turut tidak menyertainya, DAP akan menjadi satu-satunya parti komponen Pakatan Harapan yang bertanding dalam pilihan raya berkenaan
deb74b3f989e3bf4: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Besar Seri Menanti today for the swearing-in of the state executive council (exco), Harian Metro reported.
His vehicle was seen entering the palace grounds at 10.11am, after several vehicles carrying state assemblymen arrived from about 10am, the newspaper said.
The ceremony was expected to begin at 10.45am before the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Yesterday, Tuanku Muhriz received several BN leaders in audience at Istana Hinggap in Seremban.

They were Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi; deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chief Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan; Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki; and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The audience was understood to be aimed at resolving the state’s administrative crisis, which has dragged on for nearly four months, the newspaper reported.
Tuanku Muhriz had earlier revoked the appointments of the previous 10 exco members effective September 20, while Ismail stayed on as menteri besar.

The crisis deepened on November 16 when BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir announced that Ismail had resigned, which the latter denied on November 20, saying he had neither submitted nor consented to a resignation letter.
The palace has since told Ismail to show that he still commands majority support among assemblymen and to submit a list of exco members for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration.
e279f6eae327d9b4: PETALING JAYA: Six Negeri Sembilan assemblymen were sworn in as state executive council (exco) members before state ruler Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah today.
Four of the six are from Barisan Nasional (BN) and the other two are from Perikatan Nasional (PN), reported The Star.
The BN assemblymen are Umno's Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang), Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling) and Suhaimi Aini (Kota); and MCA's Koh Kim Swee (Repah).
The two PN assemblymen are Wawasan's Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas) and PAS's Fatah Zakaria (Bagan Pinang).

Negeri Sembilan has been without an executive council since Sept 20 when all 10 members were removed for allegedly breaching their oaths of office by endorsing a declaration seeking Tuanku Muhriz’s removal.
The 10 exco members comprised eight from BN and two from PN.

The 10 included Umno’s Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Razi Ali (Sungai Lui), Asna Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) and Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh).
The other three were MCA’s Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), PAS’s Fairuz Isa (Serting) and Wawasan’s Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat).

The 10 assemblymen later went to the courts to challenge their sackings, but eventually decided to withdraw the suit following Ismail Lasim's alleged resignation as menteri besar. While the Seremban High Court pointed out that Ismail’s resignation had not yet been confirmed, the 10 former exco members proceeded with the withdrawal of the suit. Tuanku Muhriz had revoked their appointments following their assertion that his purported removal in April was legitimate and that Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was the new ruler. The palace viewed their actions as inconsistent with their oath of loyalty to the ruler and the royal institution.
deb6b77d38e0710b: SYDNEY: Australia on Friday placed counterterrorism financing sanctions on two people it said orchestrated antisemitic arson attacks in Sydney and Melbourne on behalf of Iran.

Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad used a "complex chain of proxies" to attack a kosher restaurant in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in 2024, foreign minister Penny Wong said in a statement.

In August 2025, Australia ordered Iran's ambassador to leave the country, the first expulsion of its kind since World War Two. It also suspended operations at its Tehran embassy and listed the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organisation.
Wong said the new counterterrorism financing sanctions would restrict the individuals' access to funds and disrupt their ability to recruit, plan and conduct attacks.
"These sanctions are an important step in disrupting the IRGC's ability to conduct attacks against Australians and Australian interests," Wong said.
ca16648e1ae6e76b: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor state government has made a fresh call for the return of at least 25 per cent of the tax revenue contributed to the federal administration in order to strengthen the development of local facilities.

Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said that the latest call is in line with the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail’s royal decree and builds upon an initial request for 20 per cent that was submitted in December 2024.

He said the state government is currently assisting in the provision and upgrading of various facilities belonging to federal agencies, even though such matters do not fall under the state’s primary responsibilities.

“The assistance includes the repair of dilapidated police quarters in Muar, the upgrading of schools, support for emergency ward requirements and the temporary relocation of services for health clinics.
“If we had the means, the state government would certainly wish to allocate even more to support those that need assistance in Johor.

“However, this does not fall within the state government’s primary jurisdiction or core responsibilities,” he said while delivering his winding-up speech for the Johor Budget 2027 at the state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.

Onn Hafiz, who is also the Machap assemblyman, added that the state government has also provided assistance by covering payments for locum doctors, establishing the volunteer SV Healthcare Team, upgrading Sekolah Rintis Bangsa Johor (SRBJ) schools and carrying out repairs to police buildings, military camps and Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) complexes.
He further noted that this request is not new as Tunku Ismail had previously proposed that between 20 and 30 per cent of the tax revenue contributed by Johor be returned to the state.

In December 2024, the Johor government formally requested that 20 per cent of the said tax revenue be channelled back to the state, providing the state with greater fiscal space to pursue development initiatives.
The request was subsequently adjusted to at least 25 per cent, enabling the state government to plan and implement a larger number of development projects and public amenities.
4cef5fe971457453: PUTRAJAYA: Pig farmers in Tanjong Sepat will be guided through a structured transition to other more sustainable and viable agricultural activities to ensure the continuity of their income, the agriculture and food security ministry said today.
In a statement, it said potential areas identified included cattle and small ruminant farming, modern agriculture, high-value cash crops and aquaculture enterprises.
It said the initiative was being carried out through an engagement session under the Tanjong Sepat pig farmers transition programme, held here yesterday.
"Participants will be guided through a structured process to minimise the risks involved in transitioning to other agricultural subsectors or businesses," it said.
The ministry also said the initiative reflected the government's continued commitment to safeguarding the welfare of agri-food operators while driving the sustainable development of the sector.

"The ministry is mindful of the challenges faced by industry players and is confident that this transition initiative will not only provide a new lease of life for the economic sustainability of the farmers involved but also benefit the well-being of the people and the country's food ecosystem," it said.
It said the initiative was also in line with the aspirations of the National Agrofood Policy 2021-2030 and the National Food Security Policy 2030.

The programme, officiated by deputy agriculture and food security minister Chan Foong Hin, also featured information-sharing sessions and direct technical advisory services provided by the ministry and relevant departments and agencies.

They included the departments of agriculture, fisheries and veterinary services together with the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute, Farmers' Organisation Authority, Agrobank and Bioeconomy Corporation.
0523da40e5cc7477: SINGAPORE: Singapore said Friday it was "engaging" with local businesses over tightened US export controls on advanced AI chips designed by tech titan Nvidia.
But deputy prime minister Gan Kim Yong said he was unable to confirm reports that the US firm had halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries.
Citing national security concerns, the US has since 2022 restricted exports to China of Nvidia's industry-leading chips, which are used to train and run AI tools.
Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls in the wake of a scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, forcing out longtime CEO Jensen Huang before his reinstatement on Sunday.

The new US rules crack down on alleged chip smuggling to China, as well as the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.
"We are in the process of engaging our businesses, to reach out to them to see how this impacts their businesses," Gan told a local summit in Singapore on Friday.

The Financial Times and other media outlets reported Thursday, citing sources, that Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers containing its chips to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
It was unclear how long the halt would last, the reports said, but it could be a temporary measure while data centre operators seek clarity on how to obtain a newly required licence.
AFP has contacted Nvidia for comment.

The scandal surrounding the company erupted following reports of Huang's affair with Alice Huang -- a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company under investigation for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules.
Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen, is also reportedly suspected by some US officials of spying for Beijing.
Massive investments from US and Chinese tech giants have driven a data centre construction boom in Southeast Asia, especially in the countries surrounding hyper-connected Singapore.
Analysts at Fitch Ratings warned that data centre investment across Asia-Pacific would "slow and become more selective under tighter US controls over advanced AI chips" and access to computing power.

"Southeast Asian governments will face a more difficult balancing act between retaining access to advanced US technology and attracting investment from Chinese technology companies," the Fitch analysts said in a note published Thursday.

cc60a7a6b3a365c0: PETALING JAYA: The Election Commission (EC) is seeking legal clarification from the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) on the implications if Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secures a simple majority to form the state government after nominations for the Sarawak election close tomorrow.
EC chairman Ramlan Harun said the matter was still being reviewed by the AGC to ensure that any action taken complies with election regulations, Harian Metro reported.

He said all stipulated electoral processes must proceed under the current rules, and any announcement on the matter would be made only after the EC receives confirmation from the relevant authorities.
"I have asked the AGC to review this matter, and it is still under consideration. There are relevant regulations that we must comply with.

"Under the existing rules, all electoral processes must proceed as required, and any announcement will be made after that," he told a press conference after inspecting preparations for nomination day at the Samariang nomination centre in Kuching.
Ramlan said all 82 nomination centres statewide were ready to receive candidates from 9am to 10am tomorrow.

GPS has named candidates for all 82 seats, followed by Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak with 26 candidates, Parti Bumi Kenyalang and DAP with 12 each, Parti Bangsa Malaysia with one, and one independent candidate.
Of the 82 seats, 44 currently have only one candidate, 36 have two candidates and two have three candidates.

Yesterday, Sarawak civil society group Persatuan Pemangkin Daya Masyarakat, also known as ROSE, raised concerns that nearly half of the state's 82 constituencies could go uncontested in the election, following the decision by several national political parties to sit out the polls.
ROSE said preliminary estimates suggested that only about 38 seats would be contested, potentially allowing GPS to win up to 44 seats unopposed.
Barisan Nasional, PAS and Bersatu have decided not to contest the polls. With PKR and Amanah also sitting it out, DAP will be the only Pakatan Harapan component party contesting the election.
f83ba0e2e1d51f7c: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim paid tribute today to former attorney-general Abdul Gani Patail who died last night, describing him as a legal luminary who demonstrated courage in upholding justice.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said he would always appreciate Gani’s resolve in pursuing justice after Malaysia became dragged into "the biggest corruption scandal".
"He remained steadfast in his convictions throughout that difficult period, ultimately resulting in his removal from office."
Meanwhile, Sabah chief minister Hajiji Noor said Gani’s death was a huge loss, not only for Sabah, but for the entire nation.
He said Gani, as a Sabahan, made significant contributions to the legal profession and public service.
"His dedication will always be remembered," Hajiji said in a Facebook post.
Gani, who served as attorney-general from 2002 to 2015 and was the first Sabahan to hold the post, died at 9pm yesterday at the age of 71.
He was attorney-general at the height of the 1MDB scandal and was controversially removed by the government in 2015 due to "health reasons". However, Gani insisted he was in good health.
Gani was leading a special task force investigating 1MDB at the time of his dismissal.

In 2018, former prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad claimed that Gani was preparing to charge then prime minister Najib Razak over the 1MDB scandal when his contract as attorney-general was terminated.
bdbf351baad7d7c3: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today firmly denied allegations that it applies a “double standard” in its investigations, including those involving government ministries.

In a statement issued today, the MACC described the allegations as baseless, saying they did not reflect the principles of professionalism, integrity, and established procedures governing its investigations.
The commission said it had initiated an investigation on Oct 7 into expenditure related to the Rural Road Project (JALB), which involves a government ministry.
“To date, statements have been recorded from 20 witnesses from various relevant ministries and agencies to assist in the investigation.
“The investigation is ongoing, and the MACC is currently reviewing all information and evidence gathered to ensure that every aspect of the matter is investigated thoroughly,” the statement said.

The MACC acknowledged the right of all parties to express their views, criticisms, and feedback but stressed that any allegations or statements should be based on verified facts and communicated responsibly, rather than on perceptions or assumptions alone.
“The MACC wishes to emphasise that every investigation is conducted based on facts, evidence, and legal provisions, regardless of an individual’s position, rank, or background.
“The MACC remains committed to carrying out its duties professionally, independently, fairly, and transparently, while ensuring that the rule of law is consistently upheld,” the statement added.

Yesterday, media reports quoted DAP advisor Lim Guan Eng as alleging that the MACC had applied a “double standard” in its investigations into two controversies: the extension of the land lease for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), and RM2.1 billion in alleged excess expenditure by the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW). — Bernama
a391623013fba06e: KULAI, Nov 27 — MCMC’s lawsuit against Google LLC over its alleged failure to tackle harmful content on YouTube has been served on the company’s Malaysian lawyers, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
She said this was MCMC’s first lawsuit against Google. The commission had previously taken legal action against Telegram.

“To my knowledge, the suit has been served on Google, on their lawyers in Malaysia,” she told reporters after the Aspirasi Madani and Year Six appreciation programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Murni Jaya here today.
Teo said YouTube’s weak screening system forced MCMC to use its own staff to monitor and report online gambling content, when Google should have its own team to do so.
MCMC said 74,703 reports were submitted to YouTube between Jan 1 and Oct 28 this year, of which 74,569, or 99.8 per cent, concerned online gambling.
On Nov 25, MCMC announced two lawsuits against Google seeking RM600 million in total damages.
The first alleges Google failed to take reasonable steps against harmful content, including online gambling and scams.
The second concerns Papagomo’s republication of content alleged to have breached the law.
MCMC is seeking RM300 million in each suit: RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages. — Bernama
1b175bca88a1ef60: PETALING JAYA: Anwar Ibrahim mengenang ketegasan bekas peguam negara Abdul Gani Patail dalam menuntut keadilan ketika negara dilanda skandal rasuah terbesar sehingga disingkirkan daripada jawatannya.
Perdana menteri berkata pemergian Gani malam tadi menyaksikan negara kehilangan seorang tokoh perundangan yang berani menegakkan keadilan.
“Saya akan sentiasa mengenang ketegasan Allahyarham dalam menuntut keadilan tatkala negara terheret ke dalam skandal rasuah terbesar.
“Beliau teguh dengan pendirian dalam tempoh getir itu, sehingga akhirnya disingkirkan daripada jawatan,” katanya dalam kenyataan mengucapkan takziah kepada keluarga Gani.
Anwar tidak menamakan skandal berkenaan, namun perkhidmatan Gani sebagai peguam negara ditamatkan pada 27 Julai 2015 atas alasan kesihatan ketika beliau mengetuai pasukan khas menyiasat skandal 1MDB.
Gani berkhidmat sebagai peguam negara selama 13 tahun sebelum digantikan Mohamed Apandi Ali.
Sementara itu, Ketua Menteri Sabah Hajiji Noor menyifatkan pemergian Gani sebagai kehilangan besar bukan sahaja kepada Sabah, malah seluruh rakyat Malaysia.
“Sebagai anak Sabah kelahiran Lahad Datu, Allahyarham telah menabur jasa dan bakti dalam bidang perundangan serta perkhidmatan awam negara.
“Segala sumbangan dan khidmat bakti beliau akan sentiasa dikenang,” katanya.
43274bbeb910aa90: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is finalising an e-Commerce Bill to strengthen platform accountability and protect consumers from algorithmic manipulation and discriminatory pricing.
KPDN said the law will emphasise transparency, accountability, and fairness, and require platforms to disclose pricing information that affects consumers’ purchasing decisions clearly.

The ministry said the digital economy now needs more comprehensive regulation because platforms heavily influence product display, recommendations, rankings, and how prices and promotions are presented to consumers.
“In principle, using algorithms and dynamic pricing is not an offence. The technology can improve market efficiency and tailor offerings to demand and supply.

“However, consumer protection issues arise if consumers are not given clear pricing information, or if algorithms lead to misleading or manipulative practices, or cause unjustified price discrimination,” the ministry said in a written reply posted on the Dewan Rakyat website.

The ministry was responding to Dr V. Sivakumar (PH-Batu Gajah), who asked what steps would strengthen consumer protection against algorithms on e-commerce platforms, including pricing transparency and preventing price discrimination.

KPDN said the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599), including the Consumer Protection (Electronic Trade Transactions) Regulations 2024, currently governs online transactions, tackling misleading trade practices and false representations.
It added that anti-competitive uses of algorithms fall under the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712), enforced by the Malaysian Competition Commission (MyCC).
KPDN said algorithms that use personal data and user profiling are subject to the relevant ministry’s personal data protection framework.

“We will keep working with the relevant ministries and agencies so the country’s digital economy rules stay responsive to technology while consumer interests remain protected,” the ministry said. — Bernama
ea5b38468e6f6eb0: SHAH ALAM, Nov 27 — A relative wept in the courtroom today as three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers and three civilians were charged with trafficking 96.2kg of suspected methamphetamine at the RMAF Subang Air Base, the New Straits Times (NST) reported.
The six arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here under heavy police escort, with armed officers in balaclavas and tactical gear, the newspaper said.
They nodded in understanding as the charge was read out before Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin, according to the NST and Berita Harian.

They were named as Lieutenant Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, 33; Lieutenant Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, 27; Captain Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, 34; Tan Sui Seng, 48; Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin, 28; and Afifah Amdas, 34.

They are accused of jointly trafficking the drugs at the arrival foyer of the base’s Air Movement Branch at 6.50pm on November 17, under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
If convicted, they face the death penalty or, if spared the gallows, life imprisonment and at least 15 strokes of the cane.
No pleas were recorded as the case falls under the High Court’s jurisdiction, with bail not allowed and mention set for February 23 for the submission of documents, Berita Harian reported.
The daily said Nur Hanis and Afifah have yet to be represented by lawyers.
Thirteen people, including seven RMAF personnel, were detained in operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan from November 17 to 19 over a suspected drug-smuggling syndicate using air force assets.
The arrests followed the discovery of 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million during a routine inspection at the base, the NST reported.

The remaining seven suspects will face action under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985, Federal Police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said yesterday.
a5dc69e24f4897a1: SINGAPORE: JPMorgan Asset Management, BlackRock Inc and Endowus Singapore Pte are the frontrunners to manage a slice of Singapore’s S$701 billion (US$543 billion) public pension fund.

The three firms submitted proposals to run a new investment program that offers an alternative for members of the Central Provident Fund who want to earn more than the government-guaranteed return, according to people familiar with the matter. The winners will be announced in the first half of 2027.
Discussions are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.

JPMorgan would partner with Singapore’s largest bank, DBS Group Holdings Ltd, in an extension of a retirement portfolio programme that was piloted in 2024. Endowus, an investment platform, is in talks to work with Capital Group on the CPF program, said the people.

A spokesman for the CPF Board said the evaluation process is ongoing, and it can’t comment on individual applications. JPMorgan and Capital Group declined to comment. Endowus said it has been a digital adviser for investing CPF savings since 2019. BlackRock and DBS didn’t respond to requests for comment.
The investment plan was unveiled by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in this year’s budget speech as a way to deal with the country’s aging population, and will be launched in 2028.

The new programme will allow members to opt in to portfolio strategies that automatically adjust according to their age. As investors get older, the equity allocation will shift to lower-risk assets such as bonds, before being liquidated in phases by a set target date.

Currently, members have the option of manually picking investments, including bonds, stocks and unit trusts, from a list of more than 30 asset managers. As of September, just S$22 billion -- or 3% -- of net assets were invested in this optional plan, according to the CPF website.

The bulk of CPF savings are invested by the pension board in Special Singapore Government Securities. Proceeds from these securities are pooled with other government funds, including from budget surpluses and land sales, and managed by sovereign wealth fund GIC Pte for long-term returns. Members under 55 earn risk-free interest of up to 5% a year.

Founded in 1955, the CPF is Singapore’s mandatory pension fund for citizens and permanent residents to support retirement, housing and health-care needs. There are more than two million active members, and over S$14 billion in CPF contributions were received in the third quarter.
